subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof ("If n > P, every n-covector on ℝ^P vanishes, so S = 0; then S₀ := 0 satisfies (c) (both supports are empty, both densities are 0 everywhere) and (a), (b) are trivial"), with the details written out. Write d := dim L and m := n − d.
1. (Covectors of degree > P vanish.) Let k > P and α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, k), a continuous alternating k-linear form on ℝ^P. For any v_1, …, v_k ∈ ℝ^P the family (v_i) is linearly dependent because k > P = dim ℝ^P, and an alternating multilinear map vanishes on every linearly dependent family (Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent, applied to α.toAlternatingMap). Hence α = 0.
2. (Currents of degree > P vanish.) Let U ⊆ ℝ^P and T ∈ 𝒟_k(U) with k > P. Every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k is a function with values in Covector(ℝ^P, k), so ω(x) = 0 for every x by step 1; hence ω is the zero element of the submodule TestFormOn U k and T ω = T 0 = 0 because T.toCurrent is linear. By extensionality (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), T = 0. In particular S = 0.
3. (Proof of (a) and (b).) For x ∈ ℝ^P and λ ≠ 0, blowUp S x λ is a current of degree n > P in dilation x λ '' univ, hence the zero current by step 2. By definition currentEval T ω equals either T⟨ω, h⟩ or 0; for T = blowUp S x λ both are 0. Since S ω = 0 as well, currentEval (blowUp S x λ h) ω = S ω for all x, λ ≠ 0, ω. Taking x = 0 and λ > 0 gives IsConeCurrent S; taking x = −v (v ∈ L) and λ = 1 gives (b).
4. (Zero currents.) Fix a degree j and let 0 ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ j.
(i) Mass: for every W, (0).massOn W = sSup {ofReal((0)(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ j W} = sSup {0} = 0; the set is exactly {0} because it is nonempty (the zero form is admissible: tsupport 0 = ∅ ⊆ W and its Euclidean norm is 0 ≤ 1).
(ii) Integer multiplicity: the triple R₀ with carrier ∅, mult ≡ 0 and orient ≡ 0 is an IMRep univ j: ∅ is Borel and contained in univ; it is countably j-rectifiable because H^j(∅) = 0 (countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero); the constant multiplicity is measurable; mult_pos is vacuous; ∫⁻_{∅ ∩ K} mult dH^j = 0 ≠ ∞; the constant orientation is a.e. strongly measurable; the remaining a.e. condition refers to H^j⌞∅ = 0 and is vacuous. Its action is ∫_∅ (…) dH^j = 0 = (0)(ω) for every ω, so R₀ represents 0 and 0 is integer multiplicity.
(iii) Minimality: IsMinimizingIn 0 univ holds by (ii) and because (0).massOn W = 0 ≤ S'.massOn W for every competitor S' (by (i)).
(iv) Boundary: BoundaryVanishes 0 is True if j = 0; if j = j' + 1 then (0).boundary ω = (0)(dω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{j'}(ℝ^P), so (0).boundary = 0 by extensionality.
(v) Cone: for λ > 0, unfolding blowUp (restrictDomain followed by affinePushforward), every value of blowUp 0 0 λ is the zero current applied to a pulled-back test form, hence 0; so currentEval (blowUp 0 0 λ) ω = 0 = (0)(ω).
(vi) Support: (0).support = univ ∖ zeroRegion(0) = ∅. Indeed every x lies in the open ball B_1(x), whose closure B̄_1(x) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and contained in univ, and 0 vanishes on B_1(x); so x ∈ zeroRegion(0).
(vii) Densities: by (i) the quotient in HasMassDensity is 0 / (ω_j ρ^j) = 0 for every ρ (ENNReal.zero_div). As 𝓝[>] 0 is a nontrivial filter on ℝ and ℝ≥0∞ is Hausdorff, Tendsto (fun _ => 0) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ofReal θ)) holds iff ofReal θ = 0, i.e. iff θ ≤ 0. Hence HasMassDensity 0 x θ ⟺ (0 ≤ θ ∧ θ ≤ 0) ⟺ θ = 0, for every x and every degree j.
5. (Proof of (c).) Put S₀ := 0 ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ m. By step 4 (iii)–(v), S₀ is minimizing in ℝ^P, BoundaryVanishes S₀ and S₀ is a cone. By (vi), spt S₀ = ∅ ⊆ L^⊥, and, since S = 0 (step 2), spt S = ∅ as well, so for t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥ both t + y ∈ spt S and y ∈ spt S₀ are false and hence equivalent. By (vii) applied in degrees n (to S = 0) and m (to S₀): HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ⟺ θ = 0 ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ. Together with step 3 this proves (a), (b) and (c).
proof_key_steps: An alternating form of degree k > P on ℝ^P vanishes, so every test k-form is zero and every current of degree k > P is 0; hence S = 0 and all blow-ups of S are 0, giving (a) and (b).
The zero current of any degree has zero mass, is integer multiplicity via the empty IMRep, is minimizing, is a cycle and a cone, and has empty support.
For zero currents HasMassDensity x θ ⟺ θ = 0, so with S₀ := 0 both support and density equivalences of (c) hold.

subproblems.title: Invariant density function forces an invariant, n-homogeneous mass measure (μ = Θ·Hⁿ)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of S in ℝ^P (IMRep univ n, R.Represents S), μ := R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M, and L ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace. Assume that S has a density at every point (for every x there is θ_x with HasMassDensity S x θ_x) and that the density is invariant under the maps w ↦ y + λw (y ∈ L, λ > 0): HasMassDensity S w θ implies HasMassDensity S (y + λw) θ. Then (i) μ(A − y) = μ(A) (written μ((fun x => y + x)⁻¹' A) = μ(A)) for every y ∈ L and Borel A ⊆ ℝ^P; (ii) μ(λA) = λ^n μ(A) for every λ > 0 and Borel A, where λA = (fun x => λ • x) '' A.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 2 of the parent proof (μ = Θ·H^n; T6 invariance of μ), citing Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.9 and Ch. 4, Remark 1.8(2) for densities of rectifiable measures, and Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) for the upper-density estimate; the arguments are written out. Notation (all children): ℝ^P = Euclid P; H^k = μHE[k] (Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure on k-planes); ω_k = unitBallVolume k ∈ (0, ∞); for an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (carrier, mult, orient) μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^k⌞M; T_x = approxTangentPlane k M x and p_x its orthogonal projection (starProjection). The parent node's dependency im_mass_measure (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.im_mass_measure-a1, declaration dimred_im_mass_measure) gives, for an open U and R representing T in U: (a) M_W(T) = T.massOn W = μ_R(W) for open W ⊆ U; (b) x ∈ spt T iff μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 (x ∈ U); (c) all representations of T have the same measure.
1. (The density function and its invariance.) For each x choose Θ(x) with HasMassDensity S x Θ(x); thus Θ(x) ≥ 0 and S.massOn(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → ofReal Θ(x) as ρ ↓ 0. By im_mass_measure (a) (U = ℝ^P, W = B_ρ(x) open), S.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)), so μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → Θ(x). Densities are unique: if HasMassDensity S x θ and HasMassDensity S x θ', the two limits along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 in the Hausdorff space ℝ≥0∞ agree, so ofReal θ = ofReal θ', and θ, θ' ≥ 0 give θ = θ'. Consequently, for y ∈ L, λ > 0 and w ∈ ℝ^P, the hypothesis applied to HasMassDensity S w Θ(w) gives HasMassDensity S (y + λw) Θ(w), whence Θ(y + λw) = Θ(w).
2. (Preliminaries on μ.) μ = θ·H^n⌞M is a Borel measure, finite on compact sets (field locallyIntegrable_mult), hence outer regular. As θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for compact K, so ν := H^n⌞M is also locally finite, and μ and ν have the same null sets inside M. For r > 0 and x ∈ ℝ^P let η_{x,r}(z) := r^{−1}(z − x) (Chapter03.blowUpMap). H^n is invariant under isometries (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and H^n(cE) = c^n H^n(E) for c > 0 (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ / hausdorffMeasure_smul₀; equivalently the accepted DAG lemma euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables), so H^n(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n} H^n(E).
3. (Θ = θ for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M.) Let G be the set of x ∈ M such that (α) M has an approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q; then dim Q = n), and (β) ν(B̄_ρ(x))^{−1} ∫_{M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)} |θ − θ(x)| dH^n → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Property (α) holds for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M by the field orients of R. Property (β) holds for ν-a.e. x by the Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation theorem for the locally finite measure ν on ℝ^P and the locally ν-integrable function θ (Simon Ch. 1, §4; Mathlib Besicovitch.vitaliFamily with VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub, whose sets are closed balls centred at x). So H^n(M ∖ G) = 0. Fix x ∈ G.
(a) r^{−n} H^n(M ∩ B_r(x)) → ω_n as r ↓ 0. For ε ∈ (0, 1) choose continuous compactly supported f_−, f_+ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with f_− = 1 on B̄_{1−ε}(0), f_− = 0 off B_1(0), f_+ = 1 on B̄_1(0), f_+ = 0 off B_{1+ε}(0). Since η_{x,r}(M) ∩ B_1(0) = η_{x,r}(M ∩ B_r(x)), step 2 gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f_− dH^n ≤ r^{−n} H^n(M ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f_+ dH^n. By (α) the outer terms converge to ∫_Q f_∓ dH^n, which lie in [ω_n(1 − ε)^n, ω_n(1 + ε)^n] because H^n restricted to the n-dimensional subspace Q is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure (AffineSubspace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_coe_image; μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n), so H^n(Q ∩ B_s(0)) = ω_n s^n. Letting ε ↓ 0 proves (a). The same argument with B̄ gives r^{−n} ν(B̄_r(x)) → ω_n.
(b) μ(B̄_ρ(x)) = ∫_{M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)} θ dH^n = θ(x) ν(B̄_ρ(x)) + e(ρ) with |e(ρ)| ≤ ∫_{M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)} |θ − θ(x)| dH^n = o(ν(B̄_ρ(x))) = o(ρ^n) by (β) and (a). Hence μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → θ(x). For every ε > 0, μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B_{(1+ε)ρ}(x)), so the open-ball limit Θ(x) satisfies Θ(x) ≤ θ(x) ≤ (1 + ε)^n Θ(x); thus Θ(x) = θ(x).
4. (Θ = 0 for H^n-a.e. x ∉ M.) Let t > 0, R' > 0 and A := {x ∈ B_{R'}(0) ∖ M : Θ(x) > t}. Then μ(A) = 0 because μ is concentrated on M. Let ε, δ ∈ (0, 1). By outer regularity there is an open U' ⊇ A with μ(U') < ε. For each x ∈ A, μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → Θ(x) > t, so there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ U' and μ(B_ρ(x)) > t ω_n ρ^n. By the Vitali 5r-covering lemma for closed balls of radii ≤ δ (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall) there is a countable pairwise disjoint subfamily (B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i)) with A ⊆ ⋃_i B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i). Each B̄_{5ρ_i}(x_i) has diameter ≤ 10ρ_i ≤ 10δ, so the 10δ-approximating sum of the unnormalized Hausdorff measure μH[n] satisfies μH[n]_{10δ}(A) ≤ Σ_i (10ρ_i)^n ≤ 10^n (t ω_n)^{−1} Σ_i μ(B_{ρ_i}(x_i)) ≤ 10^n (t ω_n)^{−1} μ(U') ≤ 10^n ε/(t ω_n). Letting ε ↓ 0 and then δ ↓ 0 gives μH[n](A) = 0, hence H^n(A) = 0 since μHE[n] is a finite multiple of μH[n] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). Taking the union over R' ∈ ℕ and t = 1/k (k ∈ ℕ) shows H^n({x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0}) = 0.
5. (μ = Θ·H^n.) By steps 3 and 4 and Θ ≥ 0, ofReal ∘ Θ = θ·1_M H^n-a.e. Therefore for every Borel A, ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n = ∫_{A ∩ M} θ dH^n = μ(A); i.e. μ(A) = (H^n.withDensity (ofReal ∘ Θ))(A).
6. (Translation invariance, (i).) Let y ∈ L and A Borel; (fun x => y + x)⁻¹' A = A − y. The map z ↦ z + y is an isometry of ℝ^P, so it preserves H^n (IsometryEquiv.measurePreserving_euclideanHausdorffMeasure). By step 1 applied with the vector −y ∈ L and λ = 1, Θ((−y) + 1·x) = Θ(x) for every x, i.e. Θ(x − y) = Θ(x). Using step 5 and the change of variables x = z + y: μ(A − y) = ∫_{A − y} ofReal Θ(z) dH^n(z) = ∫_A ofReal Θ(x − y) dH^n(x) = ∫_A ofReal Θ(x) dH^n(x) = μ(A).
7. (Homogeneity, (ii).) Let λ > 0 and A Borel; λA = (fun x => λ • x) '' A is Borel (image under a homeomorphism). By step 2, for every Borel g ≥ 0, ∫_{λA} g dH^n = λ^n ∫_A g(λw) dH^n(w): the image of the measure H^n⌞A under w ↦ λw is λ^{−n}·H^n⌞(λA), because H^n(A ∩ λ^{−1}E) = λ^{−n} H^n(λA ∩ E) (H^n(λF) = λ^n H^n(F) for every F) (the accepted DAG lemma euclid_hausdorff_dilation_change_of_variables states this change of variables). By step 1 with y = 0 ∈ L, Θ(λw) = Θ(w). Hence, by step 5, μ(λA) = ∫_{λA} ofReal Θ dH^n = λ^n ∫_A ofReal Θ(λw) dH^n(w) = λ^n ∫_A ofReal Θ dH^n = λ^n μ(A), i.e. μ((fun x => λ • x) '' A) = ofReal(λ^n)·μ(A).
(If P < n then H^n = 0 on ℝ^P, μ = 0 and (i), (ii) hold trivially; the argument above covers this case as well.)
proof_key_steps: Densities are unique (limits in ℝ≥0∞, θ ≥ 0), so the hypothesis gives Θ(y + λw) = Θ(w) for the density function Θ, and im_mass_measure (a) turns mass ratios into μ-ratios.
At H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (approximate tangent space and Besicovitch–Lebesgue point of θ) the density is θ(x); hence Θ = θ a.e. on M.
A Vitali 5r-covering with μ(A) = 0 shows H^n{x ∉ M : Θ(x) > 0} = 0.
Therefore μ = Θ·H^n, and translation invariance and n-homogeneity of H^n with the invariance of Θ give μ(A − y) = μ(A) for y ∈ L and μ(λA) = λ^n μ(A).

subproblems.title: Stationary varifold with L-invariant n-homogeneous weight contains x and L in its tangent planes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) with μ := R.measure, and L ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace. Assume v(M, θ) is stationary in ℝ^P: R.firstVariation X = ∫_M θ·div_M X dH^n = 0 for every C¹ vector field X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support (div_M X(x) = trace(p_x ∘ DX(x))). Assume μ((fun x => y + x)⁻¹' A) = μ(A) for every y ∈ L and Borel A, and μ(λA) = λ^n μ(A) for every λ > 0 and Borel A. Then for μ-a.e. x: p_x(x) = x and p_x(v) = v for every v ∈ L, where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto T_x = approxTangentPlane n M x; i.e. x ∈ T_x and L ⊆ T_x.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof (T6: the monotonicity identity of Simon Ch. 4, 3.6 for the stationary V forces x − z ∈ T_xM a.e. for z ∈ L, then a countable dense subset of L), with the monotonicity identity derived from the first variation as in Simon Ch. 4, 3.2–3.4. Notation: μ = R.measure = θ·H^n⌞M, T_x = approxTangentPlane n M x, p_x its orthogonal projection.
1. (Constant ratios at points of L.) Let z ∈ L and ρ > 0. B̄_ρ(z) = (fun x => (−z) + x)⁻¹' B̄_ρ(0) with −z ∈ L, so μ(B̄_ρ(z)) = μ(B̄_ρ(0)) by the translation hypothesis; and B̄_ρ(0) = (fun x => ρ • x) '' B̄_1(0), so μ(B̄_ρ(0)) = ρ^n μ(B̄_1(0)) by homogeneity. Put c := μ(B̄_1(0)) < ∞ (μ is finite on compact sets by the field locallyIntegrable_mult). Then μ(B̄_ρ(z)) = c ρ^n for all ρ > 0 and all z ∈ L.
2. (Tangent planes.) For H^n-a.e. x ∈ M, hence for μ-a.e. x (μ ≪ H^n⌞M), M has an approximate tangent space Q at x (field orients); approximate tangent spaces are unique (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4: H^n⌞Q is the weak limit of the blow-ups H^n⌞η_{x,r}(M), and Q = spt(H^n⌞Q)), so T_x = Q has dimension n and trace p_x = n. By the sibling child tangent_projection_measurable (the accepted declaration imrep_univ_tangent_starProjection_aemeasurable, reused) the map x ↦ p_x is AEMeasurable with respect to μ. This is load-bearing: R.firstVariation X is a Bochner integral of θ·trace(p_x ∘ DX(x)) over M, and the measurability of x ↦ p_x makes this integrand a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by θ·|DX| (|trace(p_x ∘ A)| ≤ P‖A‖), hence integrable for compactly supported C¹ X; so the hypothesis R.firstVariation X_ρ = 0 below is the vanishing of a genuine absolutely convergent integral, which may be split into the two terms used in step 3. Fix z ∈ ℝ^P, write r(x) := |x − z| and g_z(x) := |(x − z) − p_x(x − z)|², and let h_z(x) := g_z(x)/r(x)² for x ≠ z, h_z(z) := 0; h_z is μ-measurable with 0 ≤ h_z ≤ 1, and |p_x(x − z)|² = r² − g_z(x) = r²(1 − h_z(x)) for x ≠ z.
3. (First variation identity.) Fix ε ∈ (0, 1) and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ; [0, 1]) with φ' ≤ 0, φ = 1 on (−∞, 1] and φ = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞). For ρ > 0 let X_ρ(x) := φ(r(x)/ρ)(x − z). X_ρ is C¹ (it equals x − z on B_ρ(z), and r is smooth away from z) with compact support in B̄_{(1+ε)ρ}(z). For x ≠ z, DX_ρ(x) = φ(r/ρ) I + ρ^{−1} φ'(r/ρ) r^{−1} (x − z) ⊗ (x − z), so at μ-a.e. x: div_M X_ρ(x) = trace(p_x ∘ DX_ρ(x)) = n φ(r/ρ) + ρ^{−1} φ'(r/ρ) r^{−1} |p_x(x − z)|² = n φ(r/ρ) + (r/ρ) φ'(r/ρ)(1 − h_z(x)) (near z the second term is 0 since φ' = 0 on (−∞, 1)). For ρ in a compact subinterval of (0, ∞) the integrands are C¹ in ρ with ρ-derivatives −(r/ρ²) φ'(r/ρ) and −(r/ρ²) φ'(r/ρ) h_z, bounded by a constant times the indicator of a fixed closed ball (μ-integrable); so I and J are differentiable with I'(ρ) = −∫ (r/ρ²) φ'(r/ρ) dμ and J'(ρ) = −∫ (r/ρ²) φ'(r/ρ) h_z dμ. For ρ = k ∈ ℕ, φ(r/k) h_z = 0 μ-a.e. and φ(r/k) = 1 on B̄_k(z), so h_z = 0 μ-a.e. on B̄_k(z); taking the union over k, g_z = 0 μ-a.e., i.e. p_x(x − z) = x − z for μ-a.e. x.

Notation (all children): ℝ^P = Euclid P; H^k = μHE[k] (Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure on k-planes); ω_k = unitBallVolume k ∈ (0, ∞); for an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (carrier, mult, orient) μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^k⌞M; T_x = approxTangentPlane k M x and p_x its orthogonal projection (starProjection). 0. (Translation invariance of S.) For v ∈ ℝ^P let τ_v(x) := x + v. dilation (−v) 1 (y) = v + y, so unfolding blowUp (as an affine push-forward with linear part the identity) the hypothesis says S(ω(· + v)) = S(ω) for all test ω and v ∈ L, i.e. τ_{v#}S = S, where τ_{v#}S(ω) := S(τ_v^#ω) = S(ω(· + v)).
1. (Case d = 0.) Then L = {0}, L^⊥ = ℝ^P and n − d = n. Take S₀ := S and R₀ := R, transported along n = n − 0. R₀ represents S₀; IsMinimizingIn S₀ L^⊥ is IsMinimizingIn S univ; ∂S₀ = 0; S₀ is a cone; spt S₀ ⊆ ℝ^P = L^⊥; μ₀(∅) = 0; and since H^0 = μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, ∫_{{0}} μ(A − t) dH^0(t) = μ(A). From now on d ≥ 1; put m := n − d ≥ 1.
2. (Coordinates and orientation.) Fix an orthonormal basis f_1, …, f_d of L, the orthogonal projections p : ℝ^P → L and q := I − p onto L^⊥, and coordinates t^a(x) := ⟨x, f_a⟩, so x = p(x) + q(x). Let G be the set of x ∈ M at which M has an approximate tangent space and ξ(x) orients it; H^n(M ∖ G) = 0 (field orients), and by hypothesis L ⊆ T_x for μ-a.e. x ∈ G. At such x, T_x = L ⊕ (T_x ∩ L^⊥) and dim(T_x ∩ L^⊥) = m; completing f_1, …, f_d by an orthonormal basis g_1, …, g_m of T_x ∩ L^⊥ and changing the sign of g_1 if necessary, ξ(x) = f_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ f_d ∧ ζ(x) with ζ(x) := g_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ g_m a unit simple m-vector orienting T_x ∩ L^⊥ (ζ can be chosen μ-measurable, e.g. ζ(x)(β) := ξ(x)(dt^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt^d ∧ β ∘ Λ^m q), the wedge being normalized so that (dt^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt^d ∧ γ)(f_1, …, f_d, w_1, …, w_m) = γ(w_1, …, w_m) for w_j ∈ L^⊥). The restriction of p to T_x is the orthogonal projection of T_x onto L ⊆ T_x, so the coarea Jacobian J^M p(x) equals 1. For a test n-form ω let ω♭ be the m-form ω♭(x)(v_1, …, v_m) := ω(x)(f_1, …, f_d, v_1, …, v_m) (iterated interior product; a test m-form); then ξ(x)(ω(x)) = ζ(x)(ω♭(x)) for μ-a.e. x.
3. (Slicing.) S is integer multiplicity with ∂S = 0 and locally finite mass, hence locally normal. For H^d-a.e. t ∈ L the slice ⟨S, p, t⟩ (slicing successively by t^1, …, t^d) is the integer multiplicity m-current τ(M_t, θ, ζ), M_t := M ∩ p^{−1}(t): by the coarea formula M_t is countably m-rectifiable, θ is locally H^m-integrable on M_t, and H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_t has approximate tangent space T_x ∩ L^⊥, oriented by ζ(x) (the slice orientation ξ = (∇^M t^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ ∇^M t^d)/J^M p ∧ ζ with ∇^M t^a = p_x f_a = f_a and J^M p = 1). Moreover ∂⟨S, p, t⟩ = ±⟨∂S, p, t⟩ = 0, spt⟨S, p, t⟩ ⊆ p^{−1}(t) = t + L^⊥, and by the coarea formula with Jacobian 1: S(ω) = ∫_M θ ζ(ω♭) dH^n = ∫_L ⟨S, p, t⟩(ω♭) dH^d(t) for every test n-form ω, and μ(A) = ∫_L μ_{⟨S,p,t⟩}(A) dH^d(t) for Borel A, where μ_{⟨S,p,t⟩} = θ·H^m⌞M_t. All these properties hold simultaneously for H^d-a.e. t (countably many conditions: e.g. local integrability on the balls B̄_j(0), j ∈ ℕ).

Slicing commutes with push-forward by the isometry τ_v: ⟨τ_{v#}S, p, t⟩ = τ_{v#}⟨S, p ∘ τ_v, t⟩, and for v ∈ L, p ∘ τ_v = p + v, so ⟨S, p ∘ τ_v, t⟩ = ⟨S, p, t − v⟩. As τ_{v#}S = S (step 0), ⟨S, p, t⟩ = τ_{v#}⟨S, p, t − v⟩ for H^d-a.e. t, for each v ∈ L. The slices are weakly measurable in t (t ↦ ⟨S, p, t⟩(β) is measurable for each test form β), and currents representable by integration are determined by their values on a countable family of test forms (dense in the C⁰ topology on compact sets); hence the set {(s, v) ∈ L × L : ⟨S, p, s + v⟩ ≠ τ_{v#}⟨S, p, s⟩} is measurable, and by the previous identity (with t = s + v and the measure-preserving change of variables (s, v) ↦ (s + v, v)) and Fubini it is H^{2d}-null. So for H^d-a.e. s, ⟨S, p, s + v⟩ = τ_{v#}⟨S, p, s⟩ for H^d-a.e. v. Fix such an s =: t₀ for which the properties of step 3 hold.
5. (Definition of S₀ and R₀.) Put S₀ := τ_{(−t₀)#}⟨S, p, t₀⟩ ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and R₀ := (M₀, θ₀, ζ₀) with M₀ := M_{t₀} − t₀, θ₀(y) := θ(y + t₀), ζ₀(y) := ζ(y + t₀) (transported to IMRep univ m; translation preserves Borel sets, countable m-rectifiability, local H^m-integrability and approximate tangent spaces, since η_{x−t₀,r}(E − t₀) = η_{x,r}(E)). R₀ represents S₀. M₀ ⊆ p^{−1}(t₀) − t₀ = L^⊥, so μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0; as L^⊥ is closed, every x ∉ L^⊥ has a ball of μ₀-measure 0, so x ∉ spt S₀ by im_mass_measure (b): spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥. ∂S₀ = τ_{(−t₀)#}∂⟨S, p, t₀⟩ = 0 (push-forward commutes with ∂), so BoundaryVanishes S₀ (m ≥ 1). By step 4, ⟨S, p, t⟩ = τ_{t#}S₀ for H^d-a.e. t ∈ L (write t = t₀ + v; τ_{v#}τ_{t₀#} = τ_{t#}).
6. (Product formulas.) By steps 3 and 5, for every test n-form ω, S(ω) = ∫_L (τ_{t#}S₀)(ω♭) dH^d(t) = ∫_L S₀(ω♭(t + ·)) dH^d(t) =: ([[L]] × S₀)(ω), the Cartesian product of Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.22 transported to ℝ^P = L ⊕ L^⊥ by (t, y) ↦ t + y, with [[L]] oriented by f_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ f_d (currents supported in L^⊥ with tangent planes in L^⊥ are identified with currents in L^⊥ ≅ ℝ^{P−d}). For a.e. t, τ_{t#}S₀ is represented both by the slice triple (M_t, θ, ζ) and by the translate of R₀ (carrier M₀ + t, multiplicity θ₀(· − t), orientation ζ₀(· − t)), whose measure is μ₀(· − t); by im_mass_measure (c) these measures agree: θ·H^m⌞M_t = μ₀(· − t). Hence, by step 3, for every Borel A: μ(A) = ∫_L μ₀(A − t) dH^d(t), and A − t = (fun y => t + y)⁻¹' A; this is the stated product identity (H^d restricted to L is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure on L).
7. (S₀ is a cone.) Let λ > 0 and η := η_{0,λ}, η(y) = λ^{−1}y; η maps L and L^⊥ onto themselves, η_#[[L]] = [[L]] (orientation preserved since λ > 0) and η_#([[L]] × S₀) = η_#[[L]] × η_#S₀ (η is the product of its restrictions). As S is a cone, [[L]] × η_#S₀ = η_#S = S = [[L]] × S₀. Fix ϕ ∈ C^∞_c(L) with ∫_L ϕ dH^d = 1 and a test m-form β on ℝ^P, and let ω(x) := ϕ(p(x)) (dt^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dt^d ∧ q^#β)(x), where (q^#β)(x) := β(q(x)) ∘ Λ^m q. ω is a test n-form (its support lies in p^{−1}(spt ϕ) ∩ q^{−1}(spt β), which is compact), and for t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥, ω♭(t + y) = ϕ(t) β(y) ∘ Λ^m q (in the expansion of the wedge only the term pairing dt^1, …, dt^d with f_1, …, f_d survives because q f_a = 0). For an integer multiplicity current A supported in L^⊥ with tangent planes in L^⊥, A(ω♭(t + ·)) = ϕ(t) A(β) (on L^⊥, q = id and Λ^m q is the identity on m-vectors of L^⊥; compute with a representation of A). Hence ([[L]] × A)(ω) = A(β) for A ∈ {S₀, η_#S₀}, and the identity [[L]] × η_#S₀ = [[L]] × S₀ gives (η_#S₀)(β) = S₀(β). Since dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, currentEval(blowUp S₀ 0 λ, β) = (η_#S₀)(β) = S₀(β): S₀ is a cone.
8. (S₀ is minimizing in L^⊥.) S₀ is integer multiplicity (R₀). Let W₀ be open with closure(W₀) compact, and S₀' an integer multiplicity m-current in ℝ^P with ∂S₀' = ∂S₀ = 0 (a genuine condition as m ≥ 1) and K₀ := spt(S₀' − S₀) a compact subset of W₀ ∩ L^⊥. Suppose, for contradiction, M_{W₀}(S₀') < M_{W₀}(S₀), and put δ := M_{W₀}(S₀) − M_{W₀}(S₀') > 0 (both are finite by im_mass_measure (a)). X₀ := S₀' − S₀ is an integer multiplicity m-cycle with spt X₀ = K₀ compact ⊆ L^⊥; spt S₀' ⊆ spt S₀ ∪ K₀ ⊆ L^⊥. Since m ≥ 1, the cone Y₀ := 0 ⨯ X₀ = h_#([[(0, 1)]] × X₀), h(s, y) := sy, is an integer multiplicity (m + 1)-current with compact support in L^⊥ and ∂Y₀ = X₀ − 0 ⨯ ∂X₀ = X₀ (Simon 2.31; for m = 0 there would be an extra term −X₀(1)[[0]]), and M(Y₀) < ∞. For R > 0 let Q_R := {Σ_a t^a f_a : |t^a| ≤ R} ⊆ L, oriented as L, with boundary [[∂Q_R]] := ∂[[Q_R]] (an integer multiplicity (d − 1)-cycle of mass 2d(2R)^{d−1}; for d = 1 it is the 0-current [[R f_1]] − [[−R f_1]]), and let Z_R := [[Q_R]] × X₀ − (−1)^{d−1} [[∂Q_R]] × Y₀. By ∂(A × B) = ∂A × B + (−1)^{dim A} A × ∂B (Simon 2.19), ∂X₀ = 0 and ∂[[∂Q_R]] = 0: ∂Z_R = [[∂Q_R]] × X₀ − (−1)^{d−1}(−1)^{d−1} [[∂Q_R]] × X₀ = 0. Z_R is integer multiplicity with compact support in Q_R + (spt X₀ ∪ spt Y₀). Let B be an open ball centred at 0 containing closure(W₀) ∪ spt Y₀, C_{R+1} := {Σ_a t^a f_a : |t^a| < R + 1} and W := {t + y : t ∈ C_{R+1}, y ∈ L^⊥ ∩ B}, an open set with compact closure containing spt Z_R. S + Z_R is integer multiplicity, ∂(S + Z_R) = ∂S, and spt((S + Z_R) − S) = spt Z_R is a compact subset of W; since S is minimizing in ℝ^P, M_W(S) ≤ M_W(S + Z_R). Now compute both sides. By step 6 and μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0: M_W(S) = μ(W) = ∫_{C_{R+1}} μ₀(L^⊥ ∩ B) dH^d = (2R + 2)^d μ₀(B). On W, step 6 gives S = [[C_{R+1} ∖ Q_R]] × S₀ + [[Q_R]] × S₀, hence S + Z_R = [[C_{R+1} ∖ Q_R]] × S₀ + [[Q_R]] × S₀' − (−1)^{d−1} [[∂Q_R]] × Y₀ on W, and by subadditivity of mass and M_{W₁ × W₂}(A × B) ≤ M_{W₁}(A) M_{W₂}(B) (Simon 2.20): M_W(S + Z_R) ≤ ((2R + 2)^d − (2R)^d) μ₀(B) + (2R)^d μ_{S₀'}(B) + 2d(2R)^{d−1} M(Y₀). Since S₀' = S₀ on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K₀, their measures agree there (im_mass_measure (c) applied in ℝ^P ∖ K₀ to the restricted representations), and K₀ ⊆ W₀ ⊆ B, so μ_{S₀'}(B) − μ₀(B) = μ_{S₀'}(W₀) − μ₀(W₀) = M_{W₀}(S₀') − M_{W₀}(S₀) = −δ. Therefore M_W(S + Z_R) − M_W(S) ≤ −δ(2R)^d + 2d(2R)^{d−1} M(Y₀) = (2R)^{d−1}(2d M(Y₀) − 2Rδ) < 0 for R > d M(Y₀)/δ, contradicting M_W(S) ≤ M_W(S + Z_R). Hence M_{W₀}(S₀) ≤ M_{W₀}(S₀') for every such competitor: IsMinimizingIn S₀ L^⊥.
9. Steps 1 and 5–8 give S₀, R₀ with all the stated properties.
proof_key_steps: Case d = 0: S₀ = S, R₀ = R (transported along n − 0 = n); otherwise fix an orthonormal basis of L and use L ⊆ T_x to write ξ = f_1∧⋯∧f_d∧ζ with coarea Jacobian 1 for p.
Slicing S by the projection p onto L gives integer multiplicity cycles ⟨S, p, t⟩ = τ(M ∩ p^{−1}(t), θ, ζ) with S(ω) = ∫_L ⟨S,p,t⟩(ω♭) dt and μ = ∫ μ_{⟨S,p,t⟩} dt.
Translation invariance τ_{v#}S = S and Fubini give a level t₀ with ⟨S, p, t⟩ = τ_{t#}S₀ a.e., S₀ := τ_{(−t₀)#}⟨S, p, t₀⟩; hence S = [[L]] × S₀, μ = H^d⌞L ⊗ μ₀, spt S₀ ⊆ L^⊥, ∂S₀ = 0.
Dilations commute with the product and fix [[L]], so the cone property of S passes to S₀ (test with ϕ(p x) dt∧q^#β).
Product competitors S + [[Q_R]] × X₀ − (−1)^{d−1}[[∂Q_R]] × (0 ⨯ X₀) (m ≥ 1) would beat S for large R if S₀ were not minimizing in L^⊥.

subproblems.title: Minimizing in a subspace containing the support implies minimizing (Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1, V ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace and T ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) minimizing in V (IsMinimizingIn T V: T is integer multiplicity and M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) whenever W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P is open and S is an integer multiplicity current with ∂S = ∂T and spt(S − T) a compact subset of V ∩ W) with spt T ⊆ V. Then T is minimizing in ℝ^P (IsMinimizingIn T univ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < m → IsMinimizingIn T (V : Set (Euclid P)) → T.support ⊆ (V : Set (Euclid P)) → IsMinimizingIn T univ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 9 of the parent proof (footnote 2 of Simon 7.3.1, chapter-07.txt lines 358–362: orthogonal projection onto the subspace does not increase area). Cited results: Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 (push-forward f_#T for f proper on spt T, ∂f_# = f_#∂, spt f_#T ⊆ f(spt T)) and 3.3–3.9 (the push-forward of an integer multiplicity current by a Lipschitz map proper on its support is integer multiplicity, with f_#τ(M, θ, ξ)(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω(f(x)), Λ_m d^Mf_x ξ(x)⟩ dH^m). Notation (all children): ℝ^P = Euclid P; H^k = μHE[k] (Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure on k-planes); ω_k = unitBallVolume k ∈ (0, ∞); for an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (carrier, mult, orient) μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^k⌞M; T_x = approxTangentPlane k M x and p_x its orthogonal projection (starProjection). The parent node's dependency im_mass_measure (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.im_mass_measure-a1, declaration dimred_im_mass_measure) gives, for an open U and R representing T in U: (a) M_W(T) = T.massOn W = μ_R(W) for open W ⊆ U; (b) x ∈ spt T iff μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 (x ∈ U); (c) all representations of T have the same measure.
1. (Setting.) T is integer multiplicity; fix a representation R_T = (M, θ, ξ) and μ_T := R_T.measure. Let q be the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto V and p := I − q. By im_mass_measure (b) and second countability, μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ spt T) = 0, so μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 and H^m(M ∖ V) = 0; consequently H^m-a.e. x ∈ M has its approximate tangent plane T_x contained in V (approximate tangent planes of M and of M ∩ V agree H^m-a.e. on M ∩ V, and an approximate tangent plane of a subset of V lies in V), so Λ_m q ξ(x) = ξ(x) for μ_T-a.e. x.
2. (A competitor.) Let W be open with closure(W) compact, and S an integer multiplicity m-current in ℝ^P with ∂S = ∂T and K' := spt(S − T) a compact subset of W. We must show M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S). We have spt S ⊆ spt T ∪ K' ⊆ V ∪ K', and q is proper on V ∪ K' (q^{−1}(C) ∩ (V ∪ K') ⊆ (C ∩ V) ∪ K' for compact C, as q = id on V). Hence S'' := q_#S is defined, integer multiplicity, ∂S'' = q_#∂S = q_#∂T. By step 1, q_#T = T (q_#T(ω) = ∫_M θ ⟨ω(q(x)), Λ_m q ξ(x)⟩ dH^m = ∫_M θ ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dH^m), so ∂S'' = ∂T and S'' − T = q_#(S − T), whose support lies in q(K'), a compact subset of V.
3. (The enlarged window.) A := q(W) is open in V (q : ℝ^P → V is a surjective linear map, hence open) and bounded. Choose ρ* > sup_{x∈W} |p(x)| and let W* := {t + y : t ∈ V^⊥, |t| < ρ*, y ∈ A}, the image of an open set of V^⊥ × V under the linear homeomorphism (t, y) ↦ t + y; W* is open with compact closure, W ⊆ W* (x = p(x) + q(x)), q(K') ⊆ A ⊆ W*, W* ∩ V = A and q^{−1}(W*) = q^{−1}(A). So spt(S'' − T) is a compact subset of V ∩ W*, and the minimality of T in V gives M_{W*}(T) ≤ M_{W*}(S'').
4. (Projection does not increase mass.) Let R_S = (M_S, θ_S, ξ_S) represent S and μ_S := R_S.measure. For a test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W* and Euclidean norm |ω(x)| ≤ 1: S''(ω) = ∫_{M_S} θ_S ⟨ω(q(x)), Λ_m q ξ_S(x)⟩ dH^m, and |Λ_m q ξ_S(x)| = |qτ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ qτ_m| ≤ Π |qτ_i| ≤ 1 for a unit simple ξ_S(x) = ±τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_m (Hadamard's inequality, |q| ≤ 1); hence |S''(ω)| ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(W*)) and M_{W*}(S'') ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(A)).
5. (Comparison.) S = T on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K', so μ_S = μ_T there (im_mass_measure (c) applied in ℝ^P ∖ K' to the restricted representations). Since μ_T is concentrated on V, q^{−1}(A) ∩ V = A, and W ∩ V ⊆ A (x = q(x) for x ∈ V): M_{W*}(T) = μ_T(W*) = μ_T(A) = μ_T(W) + μ_T(A ∖ W), and μ_S(q^{−1}(A)) ≤ μ_S(W) + μ_S(q^{−1}(A) ∖ W) = μ_S(W) + μ_T(q^{−1}(A) ∖ W) = μ_S(W) + μ_T(A ∖ W) (q^{−1}(A) ∖ W ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ K'). The term μ_T(A ∖ W) ≤ μ_T(closure W*) is finite. Combining with steps 3–4 and cancelling it: μ_T(W) ≤ μ_S(W), i.e. M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S) by im_mass_measure (a).
6. T is integer multiplicity and satisfies the minimality inequality for every such W and S, so IsMinimizingIn T univ.
proof_key_steps: spt T ⊆ V forces the carrier and the approximate tangent planes of T into V a.e., so q_#T = T for the orthogonal projection q onto V.
For a competitor S in W, S'' := q_#S is integer multiplicity with ∂S'' = ∂T and spt(S'' − T) ⊆ q(spt(S − T)) ⊆ V compact.
On the enlarged cylinder W* = {t + y : |t| < ρ*, t ⊥ V, y ∈ q(W)}, minimality in V gives μ_T(W*) ≤ M_{W*}(q_#S) ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(q(W))) since |Λ_m q ξ| ≤ 1.
μ_S = μ_T off spt(S − T) and μ_T lives on V; cancelling the common finite term μ_T(q(W) ∖ W) gives M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S).

subproblems.title: Supports and densities of a current whose measure is H^d⌞L ⊗ μ₀
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, L ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with d := dim L < n, S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and S₀ ∈ 𝒟_{n−d}(ℝ^P) with integer multiplicity representations R (IMRep univ n) of S and R₀ (IMRep univ (n − d)) of S₀; μ := R.measure, μ₀ := R₀.measure. Assume μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0, μ(A) = ∫_L μ₀(A − t) dH^d(t) for every Borel A (written ∫⁻ t in L, μ₀((fun y => t + y)⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[d]), and that S₀ has a density at every point of L^⊥ (for y ∈ L^⊥ there is θ with HasMassDensity S₀ y θ). Then for all t ∈ L and y ∈ L^⊥: t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀, and, for every θ ∈ ℝ, HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (L : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (S₀ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n - Module.finrank ℝ L)) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R₀ : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n - Module.finrank ℝ L)), Module.finrank ℝ L < n → R.Represents S → R₀.Represents S₀ → R₀.measure (Lᗮ : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ = 0 → (∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∫⁻ t in (L : Set (Euclid P)), R₀.measure ((fun y => t + y) ⁻¹' A) ∂μHE[Module.finrank ℝ L]) → (∀ y ∈ Lᗮ, ∃ θ : ℝ, HasMassDensity S₀ y θ) → (∀ t ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ Lᗮ, (t + y ∈ S.support ↔ y ∈ S₀.support)) ∧ ∀ t ∈ L, ∀ y ∈ Lᗮ, ∀ θ : ℝ, (HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ↔ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 10 and 11 of the parent proof (supports from the product measure; densities of products, parent C3), with the computation written out. Notation (all children): ℝ^P = Euclid P; H^k = μHE[k] (Mathlib's normalized k-dimensional Hausdorff measure, equal to Lebesgue measure on k-planes); ω_k = unitBallVolume k ∈ (0, ∞); for an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) (carrier, mult, orient) μ_R = R.measure = θ·H^k⌞M; T_x = approxTangentPlane k M x and p_x its orthogonal projection (starProjection). The parent node's dependency im_mass_measure (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.im_mass_measure-a1, declaration dimred_im_mass_measure) gives, for an open U and R representing T in U: (a) M_W(T) = T.massOn W = μ_R(W) for open W ⊆ U; (b) x ∈ spt T iff μ_R(B_ε(x)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 (x ∈ U); (c) all representations of T have the same measure. Let m := n − d ≥ 1 and λ_L := H^d⌞L, which is d-dimensional Lebesgue measure on L (isometry with Euclid d, μHE[d] = volume there); write B^L_r(c) := L ∩ B_r(c) and note λ_L(B^L_r(c)) = ω_d r^d (for d = 0, L = {0} and λ_L is the unit point mass at 0).
1. (Balls.) Let t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥ and ρ > 0. For s ∈ L, (fun y' => s + y')^{−1}(B_ρ(t + y)) = B_ρ(t − s + y). For y' ∈ L^⊥, |t − s + y − y'|² = |t − s|² + |y − y'|² (t − s ∈ L, y − y' ∈ L^⊥). Since μ₀ is concentrated on L^⊥, μ₀(B_ρ(t − s + y)) = μ₀(B_{r(s)}(y)) with r(s) := (ρ² − |t − s|²)^{1/2} if |t − s| < ρ, and = 0 otherwise. By the product hypothesis, μ(B_ρ(t + y)) = ∫_{B^L_ρ(t)} μ₀(B_{r(s)}(y)) dλ_L(s).
2. (Supports.) From step 1: μ(B_ε(t + y)) ≤ λ_L(B^L_ε(t)) μ₀(B_ε(y)) = ω_d ε^d μ₀(B_ε(y)); and since r(s) ≥ ε/2 for |t − s| < ε/2, μ(B_ε(t + y)) ≥ ω_d (ε/2)^d μ₀(B_{ε/2}(y)). Hence μ(B_ε(t + y)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0 iff μ₀(B_ε(y)) ≠ 0 for all ε > 0. By im_mass_measure (b) (U = ℝ^P) for S, R and for S₀, R₀: t + y ∈ spt S ⟺ y ∈ spt S₀.
3. (Masses of balls.) By im_mass_measure (a), S.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ(B_ρ(x)) and S₀.massOn(B_ρ(x)) = μ₀(B_ρ(x)). Hence HasMassDensity S x θ means 0 ≤ θ and μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) → θ as ρ ↓ 0, and similarly for S₀ with ω_m ρ^m.
4. (Density of S at t + y.) Let t ∈ L, y ∈ L^⊥, and let Θ₀ satisfy HasMassDensity S₀ y Θ₀ (it exists by hypothesis). Substituting s = t − ρσ (σ ∈ B^L_1(0), dλ_L(s) = ρ^d dλ_L(σ)) in step 1: (ω_n ρ^n)^{−1} μ(B_ρ(t + y)) = ω_n^{−1} ∫_{B^L_1(0)} f_ρ(σ) (1 − |σ|²)^{m/2} dλ_L(σ), where f_ρ(σ) := μ₀(B_{ρ(1−|σ|²)^{1/2}}(y)) / (ρ(1 − |σ|²)^{1/2})^m. As ρ ↓ 0, f_ρ(σ) → ω_m Θ₀ for each σ ∈ B^L_1(0) (step 3 with radius ρ(1 − |σ|²)^{1/2} ↓ 0). Since s^{−m} μ₀(B_s(y)) → ω_m Θ₀ < ∞, there is s₀ > 0 with C := sup_{0<s≤s₀} s^{−m} μ₀(B_s(y)) < ∞; for ρ ≤ s₀, 0 ≤ f_ρ ≤ C, and (1 − |σ|²)^{m/2} ≤ 1 on the finite-measure set B^L_1(0). By dominated convergence, (ω_n ρ^n)^{−1} μ(B_ρ(t + y)) → ω_n^{−1} ω_m Θ₀ ∫_{B^L_1(0)} (1 − |σ|²)^{m/2} dλ_L(σ) = Θ₀, using ω_m ∫_{|σ|<1, σ ∈ ℝ^d} (1 − |σ|²)^{m/2} dσ = ω_n (Fubini for the unit ball of ℝ^n = ℝ^d × ℝ^m: its slice over σ is an m-ball of radius (1 − |σ|²)^{1/2}). Hence HasMassDensity S (t + y) Θ₀ (Θ₀ ≥ 0).
5. (Equivalence.) Densities are unique: two limits of the same function along the nontrivial filter 𝓝[>] 0 in ℝ≥0∞ coincide, and ofReal is injective on [0, ∞). If HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ, then θ = Θ₀ by step 4, so HasMassDensity S₀ y θ. If HasMassDensity S₀ y θ, then θ = Θ₀ (uniqueness for S₀), so HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ by step 4. This proves HasMassDensity S (t + y) θ ⟺ HasMassDensity S₀ y θ for every θ.
proof_key_steps: Orthogonality and μ₀(ℝ^P ∖ L^⊥) = 0 turn the product identity into μ(B_ρ(t + y)) = ∫_{|s−t|<ρ, s∈L} μ₀(B_{(ρ²−|t−s|²)^{1/2}}(y)) ds.
Two-sided ball estimates give μ charges every ball at t + y iff μ₀ charges every ball at y; im_mass_measure (b) converts this to supports.

Source: Simon uses the approximate tangent planes T_xV of V = v(M,θ) as measurable data in all integrands of Ch. 4 (e.g. |D^⊥r|² in the monotonicity identity Ch. 4, 3.6, chapter-04.txt lines 290–312, used in parent step 3), and Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753) requires ξ to orient the approximate tangent spaces "in an H^n-measurable way". This measurability is implicit in the parent's step 3; it is proved here from Definition Ch. 3, 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86).

Notation. M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, μ = R.measure, H^n = μHE[n], ν := H^n⌞M, T_x := approxTangentPlane n M x, p_x := orthogonal projection onto T_x (starProjection), b_{x,r}(y) := r^{-1}(y − x) (blowUpMap x r).
0. Degenerate case n = 0. In the definition of approxTangentPlane, the chosen subspace in the "if" branch has finrank n = 0 (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt includes finrank Q = n), hence equals ⊥, and the "else" branch is ⊥. So x ↦ p_x is constant and measurable. Assume n ≥ 1 from now on.
1. Local finiteness. θ ≥ 1 on M, so ν(K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K (R.locallyIntegrable_mult with U = ℝ^P).
2. Tangent planes exist a.e. By R.orients there is, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (hence, as μ ≪ ν, for μ-a.e. x), an n-plane Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q; at such x the defining "if" of approxTangentPlane holds, so HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x and dim T_x = n. Let G be the set of these x; μ-a.e. x lies in G.
3. Test functions. χ(t) := max(1 − t, 0); for u ∈ ℝ^P let f_u(y) := χ(|y|²)⟨u, y⟩². f_u is continuous with support in the closed unit ball, i.e. f_u ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
4. Integrals over planes. For every n-plane Q: ∫_Q f_u dH^n = c_n |p_Q u|², with c_n := ∫_{ℝ^n} χ(|z|²) z_1² dz ∈ (0, ∞).
 Proof. Choose an orthonormal basis τ_1,…,τ_n of Q and the linear isometry ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(z) = Σ z_iτ_i, with range Q. Then H^n⌞Q is the push-forward of H^n on ℝ^n, which is Lebesgue measure L^n (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence, with a_i := ⟨u, τ_i⟩,
 ∫_Q f_u dH^n = ∫ χ(|z|²)(Σ_i a_i z_i)² dL^n(z) = Σ_{i,j} a_i a_j ∫ χ(|z|²) z_i z_j dL^n(z).
 For i ≠ j the reflection z_i ↦ −z_i is a linear isometry of ℝ^n, preserves L^n and |z|, and changes the sign of z_iz_j, so the integral vanishes; for i = j the coordinate swap z_i ↔ z_1 shows ∫ χ(|z|²) z_i² dL^n = c_n. So the integral equals c_n Σ_i a_i² = c_n|p_Q u|². Finally c_n < ∞ (continuous integrand with compact support) and c_n > 0 (the integrand is continuous, ≥ 0 and positive at (1/2, 0, …, 0)).
5. Blow-up integrals are continuous in x. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) and r > 0, and let Φ_{f,r}(x) := ∫_{b_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n (the integral occurring in HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt). Since b_{x,r} is a translation followed by the dilation by r^{-1}, H^n(b_{x,r}(B)) = r^{-n}H^n(B) for all B (translation invariance and Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀), and as in a change of variables Φ_{f,r}(x) = r^{-n} ∫_M f(r^{-1}(y − x)) dH^n(y). Let spt f ⊆ closedBall(0, R_f). For x in ball(x_0, 1) the integrand is bounded by sup|f| and vanishes unless y ∈ closedBall(x_0, 1 + rR_f), a set of finite ν-measure; it is continuous in x for each y. By dominated convergence Φ_{f,r} is continuous, hence Borel measurable.
6. Limits. For x ∈ G, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x T_x applied to f_u along r_k := 1/(k+1) → 0⁺ gives Φ_{f_u, r_k}(x) → ∫_{T_x} f_u dH^n = c_n|p_x u|² (step 4). Since μ-a.e. x lies in G, the function x ↦ c_n|p_x u|² is the μ-a.e. limit of the measurable functions Φ_{f_u, r_k}, hence μ-AEMeasurable (Mathlib aemeasurable_of_tendsto_metrizable_ae'); dividing by c_n > 0, x ↦ |p_x u|² is μ-AEMeasurable for every u ∈ ℝ^P.
7. Polarization. p_x is self-adjoint and idempotent, so ⟨p_x u, w⟩ = ⟨p_x u, p_x w⟩ = (|p_x(u + w)|² − |p_x(u − w)|²)/4. Hence x ↦ ⟨p_x u, w⟩ is μ-AEMeasurable for all u, w.
8. Assembly. With the standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P, p_x = Σ_{a,b} ⟨p_x e_a, e_b⟩ · L_{ab}, where L_{ab} ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), L_{ab}(v) := ⟨e_a, v⟩e_b (indeed p_x v = Σ_b ⟨p_x v, e_b⟩e_b and v = Σ_a ⟨e_a, v⟩e_a). A finite sum of μ-AEMeasurable scalar functions times constant continuous linear maps is μ-AEMeasurable for the Borel σ-algebra of L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P); hence x ↦ p_x = (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection is AEMeasurable with respect to R.measure.
proof_key_steps: n = 0: the tangent-plane field is identically ⊥; assume n ≥ 1.
For f_u(y) = max(1 − |y|², 0)⟨u,y⟩², ∫_Q f_u dH^n = c_n|p_Q u|² with c_n > 0 (isometry to ℝ^n and coordinate symmetries).
x ↦ ∫_{b_{x,r}(M)} f dH^n is continuous (rescaling + dominated convergence); at a.e. x it tends to ∫_{T_x} f dH^n as r = 1/(k+1) → 0.
Hence x ↦ |p_x u|² is a.e.-measurable; polarization and a basis expansion give AEMeasurable x ↦ p_x.

1. Choosing good points. μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, so the Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. property `orients` also holds μ-a.e. Together with the hypothesis: for μ-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q, and also p_x x = x. Fix such an x and an (n+1)-covector β.

2. x ∈ Q. The `if` in approxTangentPlane is satisfied (witness Q). The chosen subspace Q' satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q', and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique gives Q' = Q. So T_x = Q and p_Q x = x. An orthogonal projection fixes exactly the vectors of its range (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), so x ∈ Q.

3. Orientation data. IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q means: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q, and either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.

- The map y ↦ (ι_yβ)(τ) = β(y, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is linear in y, because curryLeft β is a continuous linear map.
- For y = τ_b, the (n+1)-tuple (τ_b, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) has equal entries at the distinct positions 0 and b+1. Since β is alternating, β vanishes on it.
- Hence the linear map vanishes on span(range τ) = Q (span induction over generators, 0, sums and scalar multiples). In particular it vanishes at y = x ∈ Q.

Source. This is the Cartan formula behind Simon's homotopy formula (Ch. 6, 2.25–2.26, chapter-06.txt lines 441–456) and Lemma 2.33 (lines 557–567), in the form used in step 6 of the parent proof: L_Xβ = d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ for X(x) = x, where L_Xβ(y) = (m+1)β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for an (m+1)-form β.

Conventions (Mathlib).
- dω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(x)).
- alt := alternatizeUncurryFin satisfies (alt f)(v_0, …, v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i f(v_i)(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_k).
- (f.curryLeft x)(v) = f(x, v).
Let B := Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y : ℝ^P →L Λ^{m+1}, and ψ(z) := β(z).curryLeft z.

1. Derivative of ψ. Φ(f, z) := f.curryLeft z is continuous and bilinear, since curryLeft is a linear isometry Λ^{m+1} → L(ℝ^P, Λ^m). Since ψ(z) = Φ(β(z), z) and β is differentiable at y, the product rule gives Dψ(y)[u] = (Bu).curryLeft y + β(y).curryLeft u. That is, Dψ(y) = K + β(y).curryLeft with K(u) := (Bu).curryLeft y.

2. dψ(y). By additivity of alt, dψ(y) = alt(Dψ(y)) = alt(K) + alt(β(y).curryLeft) = A + (m+1)β(y).
- Here A := alt(K), so A(v) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i (Bv_i)(y, v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_m).
- alt(f.curryLeft) = (m+1)f because Σ_i (−1)^i f(v_i, v_0, …, v̂_i, …) = Σ_i f(v): moving the i-th entry to the front is a cyclic permutation of sign (−1)^i (Mathlib alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft).

3. ι_y dβ(y). Let v = (v_0, …, v_m) and w := (y, v_0, …, v_m). Then dβ(y)(w) = Σ_{k=0}^{m+1} (−1)^k B(w_k)(w with w_k removed).
- The k = 0 term is B(y)(v).
- For k = i+1, removing entry i+1 of (y, v) leaves (y, v without v_i), so the term is (−1)^{i+1}(Bv_i)(y, v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_m).
Hence (dβ(y)).curryLeft y = B(y) − A.

4. Conclusion. Adding steps 2 and 3: dψ(y) + (dβ(y)).curryLeft y = A + (m+1)β(y) + B(y) − A = (m+1)·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y]. ∎

Source: step 1(c) of the parent proof of representation independence of θH^n⌞M (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3)): for an orthonormal family τ and any n-covector α, |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖; hence every unit orientation of an n-plane has norm at most 1. Norms: Covector (Euclid P) n = continuous alternating n-linear forms with the operator norm, MultiVector P n = its continuous dual with the operator norm.

1. By the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P (spanning Q; the spanning property is not used below) such that either ξ(α) = α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α.
2. Fix an n-covector α. Since α is a continuous multilinear map, |α(τ_1,…,τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_{i=1}^n ‖τ_i‖ (operator-norm bound, Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so the product is 1 (for n = 0 it is the empty product 1). Hence |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖.
3. In either sign case of step 1, |ξ(α)| = |±α(τ)| = |α(τ)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
4. Step 3 holds for every n-covector α and 1 ≥ 0, so by the defining property of the operator norm of the continuous linear functional ξ (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound) we obtain ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1. ∎
